Robot Doctor Code & OpModes

OpMode crashes with an error

Red text on the Driver Station and the OpMode stops. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 5 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does the error say "Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..."? The red error text at the bottom of the Driver Station.
  • Does the error mention null or NullPointerException? The red error text, or the robot log (Robot Controller → View Logs).
  • Does the error say "number ... is invalid"? This one appears when a motor or servo gets a value out of range.
  • Does the error mention TargetPositionNotSet? Shows up when switching to RUN_TO_POSITION too early.
  • Does it crash the moment you press INIT? Before PLAY, right as the OpMode starts.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 hardwareMap used before init

hardwareMap is null when your class fields are created, so calling hardwareMap.get there throws a NullPointerException.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Declare hardware as fields, but call hardwareMap.get inside init() or runOpMode().
  2. The robot log shows the exact line: Robot Controller → View Logs, scroll up to the red text, and find YourOpMode.java:LINE.
Get hardware inside init
public class MyTeleOp extends OpMode {
    Servo claw;                       // declare here

    @Override
    public void init() {
        claw = hardwareMap.get(Servo.class, "claw");   // get here
    }
}

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues · FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

2 Using an object that was never created

A NullPointerException means you called a method on something that is still null, like a timer or a subsystem you never made.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Find the line from the robot log (View Logs → red text → YourOpMode.java:LINE).
  2. Make sure everything used on that line was assigned first (for example timer = new ElapsedTime();).

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues · GM0 · Common software issues

3 Name in code doesn't match the configuration

"Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..." means the string in hardwareMap.get is not exactly the name in the active configuration.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Open the configuration on the Driver Station and compare names letter by letter. They are case sensitive ("leftDrive" is not "LeftDrive").
  2. Make sure the configuration you edited is the active one (its name shows on the DS main screen) and that you saved it.
  3. Watch for trailing spaces in config names.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

4 Power or position out of range

"number XXX is invalid" means setPower got something outside -1 to 1 or setPosition got something outside 0 to 1.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Clip the value before sending it with Range.clip.
  2. Look at where the value comes from. Often it is a PID output or drive math that was never normalized.
Clip values
motor.setPower(Range.clip(power, -1.0, 1.0));
servo.setPosition(Range.clip(pos, 0.0, 1.0));

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

5 RUN_TO_POSITION set before a target

TargetPositionNotSetException means you switched to RUN_TO_POSITION before calling setTargetPosition.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Call setTargetPosition first, then setMode(RUN_TO_POSITION), then setPower.
Right order
motor.setTargetPosition(1120);
motor.setMode(DcMotor.RunMode.RUN_TO_POSITION);
motor.setPower(0.5);

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues
